newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa says new Kabila government due on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa says new Kabila government due on Tuesday.

text.p: Laurent Kabila, the self-declared president of the new Democratic Republic of Congo, will announce his new government on Tuesday night, South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki said on Monday.

"A new government will be announced tomorrow night...It will be a broad-based government, as inclusive as possible of the various political forces," Mbeki, a key negotiator in the peace efforts for Zaire, told reporters in Johannesburg.

"We think this is the route to take...This is what we have been discussing," added Mbeki, who held two hours of talks with Kabila on Sunday after the rebel alliance's ousting of former president Mobutu Sese Seko after three decades in power.

Mbeki said there was a general approach among political players in the country to cooperate during the period of transition, and said he was confident that Kabila would keep to his pledge to form a widely representative government.
"I'm sure Kabila will keep his word on a new government. A process of consulation is taking place now with various leaders of other political parties and these will be formed tomorrow," he said.
Even Mobutu's party had indicated to Kabila that it would work with the new government, Mbeki said.

"It will be a broad-based government. The alliance has been greatly encouraged by communications it has received from the leadership of Mobutu's party which has said it will be willing to cooperate with the alliance."

Mbeki was the first foreign dignitary to see Kabila since the rebel leader declared himself president on Saturday. South Africa has said it will continue to offer Kabila advice on how to ensure lasting democracy and stability for African's third largest country.
